title: Delegation-safe search and filter gallery for SharePoint and Dataverse
summary: A canvas app gallery Items formula that combines text search, a choice filter and sorting while keeping every part delegable, with notes on what silently stops being delegable.
body:
A list screen with a search box, a status dropdown and a sorted gallery is the most common canvas app pattern, and also the most common source of "my app only shows 500 records" bugs. This formula keeps the whole query on the server.

## Formula (Gallery.Items)

```powerfx
With(
    {
        _q: Trim(txtSearch.Text),
        _status: ddStatus.Selected.Value,
        _me: User().Email
    },
    SortByColumns(
        Filter(
            Tasks,
            // 1) text search: StartsWith is delegable, "in" and Search are not on SharePoint
            (IsBlank(_q) || StartsWith(Title, _q)),
            // 2) choice filter: equality on a Choice column is delegable
            (IsBlank(_status) || Status.Value = _status),
            // 3) ownership toggle
            (!tglMine.Value || AssignedTo.Email = _me),
            // 4) date window: compare a column with a constant expression
            DueDate <= DateAdd(Today(), sldDays.Value, TimeUnit.Days)
        ),
        "DueDate", SortOrder.Ascending,
        "Title", SortOrder.Ascending
    )
)
```

Dropdown choices come from the column definition, not from a table scan:

```powerfx
// ddStatus.Items  (delegation-free: reads the column metadata)
Choices(Tasks.Status)
```

Count label under the gallery (no second query, no extra delegation problem):

```powerfx
// lblCount.Text
CountRows(galTasks.AllItems) & " tasks shown"
```

## How to use

1. Replace Tasks, Title, Status, AssignedTo and DueDate with your table and column names.
2. Set the gallery Items property to the formula above.
3. In Settings > General the "Data row limit" defaults to 500. Raise it only as a stopgap, never as the fix. To expose delegation problems while you build, the documentation suggests temporarily setting it to 1: every query that is not delegated then visibly returns a single row.
4. Add a TextInput named txtSearch with DelayOutput set to true, so the query runs after typing pauses and not on every keystroke.
5. Open the formula bar and check that there is no blue delegation underline on Filter, StartsWith or SortByColumns.

## Common mistakes

- Wrapping the column in a function: Filter(Tasks, Lower(Title) = Lower(_q)) is not delegable because the function runs on each row. Compare the raw column with a value.
- Using Search(Tasks, _q, "Title") on a SharePoint list. Search is not delegable there; use StartsWith, or a Dataverse table where Search is supported.
- Using the in operator against a multi-select ComboBox (Status.Value in cmbStatus.SelectedItems.Value). It works on small lists and silently truncates on large ones. Build an Or() of equality tests for a handful of values, or filter in a flow.
- Sorting by a calculated expression (SortByColumns(Filter(...), "Title" & "x")). Sort only by real columns.
- Calling Filter on a collection that was filled by ClearCollect from a non-delegated query. The collection is already truncated.

## Delegation/Compatibility notes

- Delegable here: Filter with =, <=, StartsWith, And/Or/Not around delegable tests, SortByColumns, and DateAdd with Today() evaluated as a constant.
- The With() record is evaluated once before the query, so _q, _status and _me act as constants and do not break delegation.
- Not delegable on SharePoint: Search, in, Lower/Upper/Left inside a predicate, CountRows, Sum, Average, GroupBy. On Dataverse, CountRows, Sum, Average, Min and Max over Filter are delegable (aggregates cap at 50,000 rows).
- Person columns are compared with .Email; comparing .DisplayName is slower and breaks with name changes. Whether a nested property such as AssignedTo.Email is delegated depends on the connector, so confirm there is no delegation warning (blue underline) on that line.
- Sorting by two columns: single-column SortByColumns is the documented delegable case; if the formula bar warns on the second sort column for your data source, sort by one column or accept a local sort of the filtered rows.
- Test with a list above 2,000 items. Delegation problems are invisible with demo data.

title: Save a record with Patch, IfError and Errors without losing user input
summary: A save button OnSelect formula for canvas apps that creates or updates a record, shows the real server error, keeps the form filled on failure and only navigates on success.
body:
A save button that always shows "Saved!" is a bug generator. Patch can fail because of permissions, required columns, conflicts or throttling. IfError lets you separate the failure path from the success path and keep what the user typed.

## Formula (btnSave.OnSelect)

```powerfx
UpdateContext({locSaving: true});

IfError(
    Set(
        varSaved,
        Patch(
            Expenses,
            If(IsBlank(varEdit), Defaults(Expenses), varEdit),
            {
                Title: Trim(txtTitle.Text),
                Amount: Value(txtAmount.Text),
                'Expense Date': dpDate.SelectedDate,
                Category: cmbCategory.Selected,
                Notes: txtNotes.Text
            }
        )
    ),
    // failure path: stay on screen, show the first error
    Notify(
        "Could not save: " & FirstError.Message,
        NotificationType.Error,
        6000
    ),
    // success path (DefaultResult): runs only when nothing above failed
    Notify("Expense saved", NotificationType.Success);
    UpdateContext({locSaving: false});
    Set(varEdit, Blank());
    Navigate(scrExpenseList, ScreenTransition.Fade)
);

UpdateContext({locSaving: false})
```

Disable the button while saving and while input is invalid:

```powerfx
// btnSave.DisplayMode
If(
    locSaving || Len(Trim(txtTitle.Text)) = 0 || !IsNumeric(txtAmount.Text),
    DisplayMode.Disabled,
    DisplayMode.Edit
)
```

Alternative when you want every error of a data source, for example after a loop of Patch calls:

```powerfx
If(
    !IsEmpty(Errors(Expenses)),
    Notify(
        "Save failed for " & CountRows(Errors(Expenses)) & " record(s): " &
        First(Errors(Expenses)).Message,
        NotificationType.Error
    )
)
```

## How to use

1. Set varEdit to the selected gallery item when the user opens the edit screen, or to Blank() for a new record.
2. Give the inputs Default values from varEdit (for example txtTitle.Default = varEdit.Title) so edit and create share one screen.
3. Paste the OnSelect formula on the button. Adjust table and column names.
4. Test failure on purpose: remove your write permission or leave a required Dataverse column empty and confirm the error text appears and the inputs keep their values.

## Common mistakes

- Placing Navigate directly after Patch. Navigate runs even when Patch failed, and the user loses the typed input.
- Reading Errors() before the Patch call. Errors reflects the last operation on that data source, so read it right after.
- Value(txtAmount.Text) on an empty or non-numeric box produces an error that IfError will catch with a confusing message. Validate with IsNumeric first or wrap in IfError(Value(...), 0).
- Using Patch to create without Defaults(). Patch(Expenses, {Title: "x"}) is not a valid create call; the base record must be Defaults(Expenses).
- Forgetting that in locales with a decimal comma the chain operator is ;; instead of ;.

## Delegation/Compatibility notes

- Patch, Defaults, IfError, FirstError, Errors and Notify are available in all canvas apps. FirstError is only valid inside the replacement arguments of IfError.
- For Choice columns on SharePoint pass the whole choice record (cmbCategory.Selected). On Dataverse choice columns pass the enum value, for example 'Category (Expenses)'.Travel.
- Patch returns the saved record including server-generated values such as ID and Created, which is why the result is stored in varSaved.

title: Concurrent screen load and batch Patch with ForAll for faster canvas apps
summary: Formulas to load several data sources in parallel with Concurrent and write a staged collection back in one pass with Patch and ForAll, including per-row error reporting.
body:
Two things make canvas apps feel slow: loading data sources one after another, and saving rows one click at a time. Concurrent and a staged collection fix both.

## Load reference data in parallel (Screen.OnVisible)

```powerfx
Concurrent(
    ClearCollect(colProjects, Filter(Projects, Active = true)),
    ClearCollect(colCategories, Choices(Expenses.Category)),
    ClearCollect(colMyOpen, Filter(Tasks, AssignedTo.Email = User().Email, Status.Value <> "Done")),
    Set(varMe, LookUp(Employees, Email = User().Email))
)
```

Arguments that contain connector or Dataverse calls can run at the same time, and the formula continues when all of them finish. How many really run in parallel depends on the device or browser. Do not put anything in Concurrent that depends on a sibling argument (for example a Filter on colProjects) because the order is not guaranteed.

## Stage rows locally, then save them in one pass

Collect lines while the user edits, no network involved:

```powerfx
// btnAddLine.OnSelect
Collect(
    colLines,
    {
        Product: cmbProduct.Selected.Name,
        Qty: Value(txtQty.Text),
        Price: cmbProduct.Selected.Price
    }
);
Reset(txtQty)
```

Save the header first, then all lines with one Patch call:

```powerfx
// btnSubmit.OnSelect
Set(
    varOrder,
    IfError(
        Patch(Orders, Defaults(Orders), {Customer: cmbCustomer.Selected, 'Order Date': Today()}),
        Notify("Order header failed: " & FirstError.Message, NotificationType.Error); Blank()
    )
);
If(
    !IsBlank(varOrder),
    IfError(
        Patch(
            OrderLines,
            ForAll(colLines, Defaults(OrderLines)),
            ForAll(
                colLines As L,
                {
                    Order: varOrder,
                    Product: L.Product,
                    Quantity: L.Qty,
                    'Unit Price': L.Price
                }
            )
        ),
        Notify("Some lines failed: " & FirstError.Message, NotificationType.Error),
        Clear(colLines);
        Notify("Order " & varOrder.'Order Number' & " submitted", NotificationType.Success);
        Navigate(scrOrders)
    )
)
```

Update many existing rows (for example "close all selected"):

```powerfx
ForAll(
    galTasks.AllItems As T,
    If(T.chkSelect.Value, Patch(Tasks, LookUp(Tasks, ID = T.ID), {Status: {Value: "Done"}}))
);
Refresh(Tasks)
```

## How to use

1. Put the Concurrent block on App.OnStart only for data every screen needs; otherwise load per screen in OnVisible.
2. Keep colLines columns identical to the target columns you map, so the mapping stays readable.
3. After submit, call Refresh on the data source to see server-calculated values.

## Common mistakes

- Using Collect(OrderLines, ...) in a ForAll loop for hundreds of rows. One Patch call with a table of base records and a table of change records is usually faster than one call per row; measure it for your data source.
- Reading colLines inside the ForAll that clears it. Clear after the Patch succeeded, never before.
- Expecting ForAll to be ordered or transactional. If line 3 fails, lines 1 and 2 are already saved. Use the error handling above, or make the operation idempotent with a status column.
- Setting a variable in one Concurrent branch and reading it in another. Not supported reliably.

## Delegation/Compatibility notes

- Filter(Projects, Active = true) and Filter with AssignedTo.Email are delegable on Dataverse and SharePoint; the Status.Value <> "Done" test is delegable on Dataverse; on SharePoint check the delegation warning for your column type and switch to a positive test if it appears.
- LookUp is delegable; ClearCollect stores at most the data row limit (500 by default, adjustable in Settings > General).
- Concurrent is only for behavior formulas, needs at least two arguments, and its arguments must not depend on each other. The Microsoft reference shows it with Set and ClearCollect and says nothing about Navigate, so keep Navigate and anything that needs a sibling result outside the block.
- Patch with tables is a documented Power Fx form: base records and change records must match one-for-one or an error occurs, and the result is a table. Speed and support depend on the connector, so test it on your data source and fall back to Patch per row if your connector rejects the table form.

title: Role-based screens and buttons in a canvas app using a user lookup
summary: Formulas that map User().Email to a role in a Dataverse or SharePoint table, guard screens, enable or hide buttons and filter rows by ownership, plus the limits of client-side checks.
body:
Canvas apps have no built-in role system. The usual pattern is an AppUsers table with Email and Role columns, looked up once and referenced everywhere.

## Define the role once (App.Formulas)

```powerfx
curUser = LookUp(AppUsers, Email = Lower(User().Email));
isAdmin = !IsBlank(curUser) && curUser.Role.Value = "Admin";
isManager = !IsBlank(curUser) && curUser.Role.Value in ["Admin", "Manager"];
isKnownUser = !IsBlank(curUser) && curUser.Active = true;
```

## Guard a screen (Screen.OnVisible of the admin screen)

```powerfx
If(
    !isAdmin,
    Notify("You do not have access to this page.", NotificationType.Warning);
    Navigate(scrHome, ScreenTransition.None)
)
```

## Control visibility and state

```powerfx
// btnDelete.Visible
isAdmin

// btnApprove.DisplayMode
If(
    isManager && ThisItem.Status.Value = "Pending" && ThisItem.Requester.Email <> User().Email,
    DisplayMode.Edit,
    DisplayMode.Disabled
)

// navAdmin.Visible  (menu item)
isManager
```

The last condition in btnApprove enforces four-eyes: nobody approves their own request.

## Filter rows by role

```powerfx
// galRequests.Items
SortByColumns(
    Filter(
        Requests,
        isManager || Requester.Email = User().Email
    ),
    "Created", SortOrder.Descending
)
```

## Friendly landing logic (App.StartScreen)

```powerfx
If(isKnownUser, scrHome, scrNoAccess)
```

## How to use

1. Create AppUsers with Email (text), Role (choice: Admin, Manager, User) and Active (yes/no).
2. Paste the App.Formulas block. Because named formulas are lazy and re-evaluated, you do not need App.OnStart.
3. Use the named values in Visible, DisplayMode and Items properties.
4. Add a no-access screen with a contact address, so a user who is not in the table knows who to ask.

## Common mistakes

- Treating this as security. Hiding a button does not stop a user from calling the data source with another app or the API. The real protection must be in the data layer: Dataverse security roles and row ownership, or SharePoint item permissions. The formulas above only shape the user experience.
- Comparing User().FullName. Names change and collide; use the email address and lower-case both sides.
- Using a Person column with .DisplayName in a filter. Use .Email.
- Putting the role lookup inside every control. Resolve it once so the table is queried once.
- Forgetting a blank case: when curUser is blank, curUser.Role.Value is blank and comparisons fail quietly; the IsBlank guard makes it explicit.

## Delegation/Compatibility notes

- Filter with an Or of a constant (isManager) and a column test is delegable on Dataverse; on SharePoint the analyzer may warn on Or across a constant. If it does, switch with If(isManager, Requests, Filter(Requests, Requester.Email = User().Email)) which keeps each branch simple and delegable.
- The in operator with a literal table of text values is evaluated locally on curUser.Role.Value, not against the data source, so it is safe here.
- For groups from Microsoft Entra ID, check membership in a Power Automate flow or the Office 365 Groups connector and cache the result in a variable; do not call it per control.

title: Model-driven command bar buttons with Power Fx and the Self.Selected object
summary: Command bar formulas for model-driven apps: visibility rules and OnSelect actions that patch the selected record or all selected grid rows, notify the user and refresh the view.
body:
Model-driven apps can run Power Fx from the command bar, so a no-code maker can add a button that previously needed JavaScript and a ribbon editor.

## Where to put it

In the app designer open the table, choose Edit command bar, pick Main grid, Main form or Subgrid, add a Command, choose Run Power Fx and set Visibility and OnSelect as below. Save and publish.

## Visibility formulas

```powerfx
// Show the button only when at least one row is selected in the grid
CountRows(Self.Selected.AllItems) > 0

// Show the button on a form only for a saved record that is not on credit hold
!IsBlank(Self.Selected.Item) && Self.Selected.Item.'Credit Hold' = false

// The record decides, not the user: show Remove credit hold only when the hold is set
!IsBlank(Self.Selected.Item) && Self.Selected.Item.'Credit Hold' = true
```

Role-based visibility is not possible with a LookUp on User(): the Microsoft documentation lists User among the functions that are not supported in command bar formulas. Control who may use an action with Dataverse security roles instead; a user without write access to the table cannot run the Patch anyway.

## OnSelect: patch the record on a form

```powerfx
Patch(Accounts, Self.Selected.Item, {'Credit Hold': true});
Notify("Account " & Self.Selected.Item.'Account Name' & " placed on credit hold")
```

## OnSelect: bulk action on selected grid rows

```powerfx
With(
    {_rows: Self.Selected.AllItems},
    IfError(
        ForAll(_rows As R, Patch(Accounts, R, {'Credit Hold': true})),
        Notify("Could not update all rows: " & FirstError.Message, NotificationType.Error),
        Notify(CountRows(_rows) & " account(s) updated");
        Refresh(Accounts)
    )
)
```

## OnSelect: guard against unsaved changes on a form

Self.Selected.Unsaved is documented to return false whenever AutoSave is true, which is the default, so this guard only matters when auto-save is off. Notify in the command bar supports the Error, Warning and Information types; NotificationType.Success is shown as informational.

```powerfx
If(
    Self.Selected.Unsaved,
    Notify("Save the record first, then run this action.", NotificationType.Warning),
    Patch(Accounts, Self.Selected.Item, {'Credit Hold': false});
    Notify("Credit hold removed")
)
```

## OnSelect: open an external page with record context

```powerfx
Launch("https://example.com/accounts/" & Self.Selected.Item.Account)
```

## How to use

1. Use the logical display names that appear in your environment (for example 'Account Name'); IntelliSense in the formula bar lists them.
2. Test on a copy of the app in a development environment, because Patch writes real data.
3. For groups of related changes prefer a Dataverse custom API or a flow, so the logic is centrally governed and reusable.

## Common mistakes

- Using functions the command bar does not support. The documentation lists, among others, Set, UpdateContext, Collect, Clear, SaveData, LoadData, ResetForm, SubmitForm, Back and User as unsupported; the formula bar flags them. Navigate is supported but takes pages, tables and records (for example Navigate(Accounts)), not canvas screens.
- Expecting Self.Selected.Item to be filled everywhere. It is blank when nothing is selected or when SelectionMax is not 1. In a grid with multi-select use Self.Selected.AllItems; on a form use Self.Selected.Item.
- Forgetting Refresh. A Patch run from the command bar updates data, but the grid may show the previous values until refreshed.
- Making the Visibility formula expensive. It re-evaluates as selection changes; avoid LookUp against large tables there, or cache the result with a column on the user table.
- Skipping error handling on bulk updates. ForAll does not roll back earlier rows.

## Delegation/Compatibility notes

- Patch, Notify, Launch, Navigate and Confirm are listed as supported in the documentation. ForAll, With, IfError and Refresh are not mentioned either way, so confirm them in the formula bar (they are commonly used in command formulas). Self.Selected.Item, AllItems, State and Unsaved are the command-specific properties.
- Patch on Dataverse needs no delegation; the With() record in the bulk example is evaluated once.
- Command bar Power Fx needs Dataverse tables and a model-driven app in the modern app designer; availability of individual functions can change by release, so check the formula bar messages.

title: KPI tiles and grouped summaries with CountRows, Sum, GroupBy and AddColumns
summary: Formulas for dashboard tiles and a ranked summary table in canvas apps, with clear guidance on which aggregates are delegable on Dataverse and which need a collection or a flow on SharePoint.
body:
Dashboards in canvas apps are mostly aggregation. The trick is knowing which aggregations run on the server and which pull rows to the device.

## Tiles (one formula per Label.Text)

```powerfx
// Open orders
Text(CountRows(Filter(Orders, Status.Value = "Open")), "#,##0")

// Revenue last 30 days
Text(
    Coalesce(
        Sum(Filter(Orders, 'Order Date' >= DateAdd(Today(), -30, TimeUnit.Days)), Amount),
        0
    ),
    "$#,##0"
)

// Average order value
Text(IfError(Average(Filter(Orders, Status.Value = "Won"), Amount), 0), "$#,##0.00")
```

## Change versus previous period without divide-by-zero

```powerfx
With(
    {
        _cur: Coalesce(Sum(Filter(Orders, 'Order Date' >= DateAdd(Today(), -30, TimeUnit.Days)), Amount), 0),
        _prev: Coalesce(
            Sum(
                Filter(
                    Orders,
                    'Order Date' >= DateAdd(Today(), -60, TimeUnit.Days),
                    'Order Date' < DateAdd(Today(), -30, TimeUnit.Days)
                ),
                Amount
            ),
            0
        )
    },
    If(_prev = 0, "n/a", Text((_cur - _prev) / _prev, "+0.0%;-0.0%"))
)
```

## Fixed categories: one count per category (delegable on Dataverse)

```powerfx
// Screen.OnVisible
ClearCollect(
    colByStatus,
    ForAll(
        ["New", "Open", "Won", "Lost"] As S,
        {Status: S.Value, Orders: CountRows(Filter(Orders, Status.Value = S.Value))}
    )
)
```

## Group a local collection, rank and show a table

```powerfx
// Load a bounded slice first
ClearCollect(colRecent, Filter(Orders, 'Order Date' >= DateAdd(Today(), -90, TimeUnit.Days)));

// galRegions.Items
SortByColumns(
    AddColumns(
        GroupBy(colRecent, "Region", "Rows"),
        "Total", Sum(Rows, Amount),
        "Orders", CountRows(Rows),
        "Average", Average(Rows, Amount)
    ),
    "Total", SortOrder.Descending
)
```

Gallery labels then read ThisItem.Region, Text(ThisItem.Total, "$#,##0") and ThisItem.Orders.

## How to use

1. Put the fixed-category and collection formulas in Screen.OnVisible, and show a spinner variable while they run.
2. Keep tiles on the server (Filter with Sum or CountRows) when your source is Dataverse.
3. If Dataverse aggregates are heavy, create a rollup column or a view and read that.

## Common mistakes

- Summing a collection that was truncated at the data row limit (500 by default) and presenting it as a total. The number looks right and is wrong.
- Using GroupBy directly on a SharePoint list. GroupBy is not delegable; load a bounded slice into a collection first as above, and label the tile with its time window.
- Distinct(Orders, Status.Value) on a large table to build categories. Use a fixed list or Choices().
- Dividing without a guard. Use If(_prev = 0, ...) or IfError.
- Formatting numbers with locale-specific separators by hand. Use Text with a format string and, if needed, a language tag such as "[$-en-US]".

## Delegation/Compatibility notes

- Dataverse: CountRows, Sum, Average, Min and Max over a Filter are delegable (aggregate functions work up to 50,000 records); GroupBy and Distinct are not.
- SharePoint: Filter with =, <, >= and StartsWith are delegable; CountRows, Sum, Average, GroupBy and Distinct are not. For exact totals use a Power Automate flow, a SharePoint view with totals, or push aggregation to Power BI.
- AddColumns, GroupBy and ForAll on collections run locally and have no delegation limits beyond what is already in the collection.

title: Call a Power Automate flow from a canvas app and parse JSON with ParseJSON
summary: Run a flow with JSON built from a collection, handle failures with IfError and turn the untyped JSON response into a typed collection using ParseJSON, Table, Text and Value.
body:
Flows are the escape hatch for anything a canvas app cannot do on its own: approvals, long calculations, calling an API with a secret, sending mail. The app side is three steps: send JSON, receive text, parse.

## Send data to the flow

Add the flow to the app (Power Automate pane), trigger "Power Apps (V2)" with a text input named payload, and a "Respond to a Power App or flow" action with a text output named result. In the app:

```powerfx
// btnRun.OnSelect
UpdateContext({locBusy: true});
Set(
    varReply,
    IfError(
        PriceCheck.Run(
            JSON(colLines, JSONFormat.Compact)
        ),
        Notify("The price check failed: " & FirstError.Message, NotificationType.Error);
        Blank()
    )
);
UpdateContext({locBusy: false})
```

PriceCheck is the flow name as added to the app; colLines is a collection such as {Sku: "A-100", Qty: 3}. JSON() turns a table into a JSON array; JSONFormat.Compact removes whitespace.

## Parse the response

Suppose the flow returns text like {"currency":"EUR","items":[{"sku":"A-100","price":12.5,"inStock":true}]}:

```powerfx
// still in btnRun.OnSelect, after the call
If(
    !IsBlank(varReply),
    With(
        {_json: ParseJSON(varReply.result)},
        Set(varCurrency, Text(_json.currency));
        ClearCollect(
            colPrices,
            ForAll(
                Table(_json.items) As I,
                {
                    Sku: Text(I.Value.sku),
                    Price: Value(I.Value.price),
                    InStock: Boolean(I.Value.inStock)
                }
            )
        )
    )
)
```

Guard against missing fields so a changed response does not crash the screen:

```powerfx
Price: IfError(Value(I.Value.price), 0),
Sku: Coalesce(Text(I.Value.sku), "unknown")
```

Show the typed result in a gallery: galPrices.Items = colPrices, labels use ThisItem.Sku and Text(ThisItem.Price, "#,##0.00") & " " & varCurrency.

## How to use

1. Make the flow return a single text output containing JSON; that is the most stable contract for the app.
2. Treat the response as untyped: every field read goes through Text(), Value(), Boolean() or DateValue().
3. Use a loading flag (locBusy) on a spinner, and disable btnRun while it is true so users cannot double-run the flow.
4. Keep the flow fast. A flow called from an app is synchronous from the user view, and long runs time out; for long jobs return immediately with a job id and poll or notify.

## Common mistakes

- Reading a field of ParseJSON without a conversion. Untyped values cannot be used directly in a label or a comparison.
- Passing a collection straight into Run(). Flow parameters are text, number, yes/no, file or a few more simple types, so serialise with JSON().
- Using ParseJSON on an empty string. Check IsBlank first.
- Embedding secrets such as API keys in the app. Keep them in the flow (connection or environment variable) and let the app call the flow.
- Forgetting that every user of the app needs permission to run the flow; with shared connections review who can run it.

## Delegation/Compatibility notes

- ParseJSON, Text, Value, Boolean and JSON are documented Power Fx functions available in canvas apps. Table() over an untyped array returns a single-column table named Value, which is why the loop reads I.Value.sku; this form appears in the Microsoft ParseJSON reference. ForAll directly over the array, without Table(), also works and then reads ThisRecord.sku. Use the form your formula bar accepts.
- Flow calls and data source calls are asynchronous operations; do not use them in properties that re-evaluate often, such as Items of a gallery. Run them from OnSelect or OnVisible and store the result.
- Flows triggered from Power Apps need a premium license only if they use premium connectors.
